segments: The 71st year of the Greeks {OCR?}:
sent some of his forces into the land of the Persians,
and they devastated, took captive, and returned.
Now the Persian Marzban who was in Nisibis devised a plan,
and went out to Marcian.
And he delayed him for four months,
pretending that they would inform their king,
so that he might peacefully restore Nisibis,
and if not, behold, war was before them.
And during this delay they brought provisions into Nisibis,
and they cut down the orchards around it to the distance of a bowshot,
and expelled the Christians from the city.
Then the emperor wrote to Marcian,
that without delay he should encamp against Nisibis.
And when he encamped,
he set up against it battering rams and war engines,
and built high towers,
and invested the city in great distress.
The emperor, however, by reason of some cause which we shall relate later, became enraged at Marcian,
and sent Acacius, a boorish and harsh man, to remove Marcian,
and to take his place himself.
And when he arrived,
he seized Marcian and sent him to Dara.
Now when the forces saw this,
they supposed that the emperor had died,
and that another had perhaps tyrannically usurped rule over the Romans;
therefore they abandoned their camps and fled.
And the Persians came out from Nisibis,
and plundered their camps.
Then Khosrow, when he heard that the Romans had fled,
came and took the siege engines, the ballistas, and the rest of the war apparatus that the Romans had left behind,
and encamped against the city of Dara.
And he waged war against it for six months,
and was not able to subdue it.
And he demanded from them five quintals of gold so that he would depart from them.
However, that comes {commissioner} who was sent with him did not inform them.
Then Khosrow became even more enraged,
and by means of wooden ladders the Persians climbed up on the wall.
The Romans, however, fought for seven days,
and did not allow any of the Persians to descend into the city.
Then Khosrow said to them:
"Come, let us make peace,
for behold, many are being killed from us and from you."
And when those wretched people believed the oath of the Persians, they laid down their weapons,
and the two sides mingled together.
And the Persians laid hands upon the Romans,
and slaughtered among them one hundred and fifty thousand souls,
and ninety thousand they led away into captivity.
And they collected about two hundred quintals of gold.
Then Khosrow said to the Roman leaders:
"Fools, why did you not give five out of two hundred,
and avert all these things?" [p. 83]
